turn_text: We know that in Wisconsin, dairy is a major part of our agriculture sector. But that dairy farmers have faced significant headwinds, both man-made as well as mother nature, whether that's extreme weather and flooding or whether that's trade issues like we were just discussing, whether that sharp increases in inputs or getting on the other end just a low price for the milk produced. We've seen a lot of small, medium-sized dairy farms go under. That's a result of these significant challenges. So I was so proud to champion the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative in the last Farm Bill. And as a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, I've been a champion for fully funding it, allowing both producers and processors to add value or create new efficiencies on the farm. If you create new efficiencies, obviously, you're cutting your expenses and increasing profits. If you're creating a new product or adding value to what you do, another way of increasing the bottom line, we have seen small and medium sized dairy farms and small and medium sized processing operations really leap at the opportunity to innovate and to apply for this funding. And our dairy industry supports over 150,000 jobs in Wisconsin. It's a big deal. And to be able to have the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative thriving is important to support our farmers.
